reason: E2 and E3 show that Al addition can promote protective Al2O3 scales and improve oxidation resistance in some alloys, but neither addresses refractory high-entropy alloys at the specified conditions. E1 directly shows that in a refractory high-entropy alloy at 1000–1100 °C, Al2O3 was not continuous and did not provide an effective barrier, contradicting the key premise that 2–3 at.% Al will form a protective scale in this context. The cited evidence thus provides only partial, generic support while the most relevant study contradicts the mechanism.
premises: Al addition promotes formation of a continuous, protective Al2O3 scale in high-entropy alloys
A continuous Al2O3 scale acts as an effective barrier against oxidation
2–3 at.% Al is sufficient to form such a protective scale in refractory high-entropy alloys
Cr-based oxide scales in refractory high-entropy alloys are non-protective and porous
